report:
Reviewed the complete claim, ordinary sage_ir::ty implementation association and whole ty.rs, and the complete single associated TODO test sage_meta::todo::types_lifetimes_unchecked_borrows. Independently verified exact byte equality of current ty.rs and representation_spec.rs against the historical implementation_sources/test_sources; the historical rationale is consistent with current evidence, not execution proof.

The claim requires Outlives(Dummy, Dummy), explicit reference/dereference operations preserving ordinary typing, and absence of borrow liveness, uniqueness, overlap and validity checking. Lifetime has only Dummy and explicitly documents deferred lifetime inference/borrow checking; Ty::Ref retains referent type and mutability, so lifetime erasure does not erase ordinary reference types. This representation is consistent with the claim but alone does not prove outlives evaluation or expression checking behavior. Those operational and acceptance scenarios remain deferred verification, not inferred successes.

The sole associated test has no assertions and explicitly reserves negative fixtures for programs rejected only by lifetime or borrow rules. This adequately preserves the intentional acceptance gap for liveness, uniqueness, overlap and validity, including Dummy outlives behavior and the distinction from ordinary reference/dereference type errors. Completing it requires concrete well-typed reference/dereference fixtures that violate each borrow-only restriction, assertions that Sage accepts them, and ordinary type-error controls; unified lifetime/borrow checking itself is not a prerequisite to testing intentional acceptance. The prior deferral remains justified and visible; no behavioral coverage or full implementation completion is claimed from the empty test. No N/A evidence exists.

Read the review decisions policy through review read. Personally executed review start, exact baseline comparison and review read, then record; no Rust edits, build or behavioral tests were performed. Coordinator-reported 321 sage-meta tests and root build are separate baseline execution and are not evidence that this TODO ran meaningful assertions. No additional source helpers were relied upon.
